Explanatory Analysis: Women, Business and the Law (Mobility)¶

Name: Dhakshitha Mohan Rao
ID: GH1044699
Dataset: World Bank WBL - Mobility Topic

The Audience: Global Policy Makers, Human Rights NGOs, and International Development Funds.
The Objective: To visually expose legal barriers restricting women's freedom of movement, driving targeted policy reform and advocacy where it is needed most.

In [ ]:

1. The Regional Divide in Freedom of Movement¶

While high-income economies have dismantled legal barriers, the Middle East & North Africa (MENA) remain severely restricted.

In [ ]:
# Step 1: Data Setup (Using the aggregates from the dataset)
regions = [
    'High income', 'Europe & Central Asia', 'Latin America & Caribbean',
    'East Asia & Pacific', 'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'South Asia', 'Middle East & North Africa'
]
scores = [100.0, 91.5, 89.2, 82.4, 73.8, 62.1, 40.5] # Data based on 2024 WBL averages

# Step 2: Initialize layout
fig, (ax_plot, ax_text) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 7), gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [2.5, 1]})

# Step 3: Define a high-contrast color palette
# We use a gradient from "Success" (Purple/Green) to "Critical" (Red)
colors = ['#6C5CE7', '#00B894', '#0984E3', '#FDCB6E', '#E17055', '#D63031', '#8B0000']

# Step 4: Render horizontal bars
bars = ax_plot.barh(regions, scores, color=colors, height=0.7, edgecolor='white', linewidth=1)

# Step 5: Styling & Data Labels
ax_plot.set_xlim(0, 115)
ax_plot.invert_yaxis() # Highest scores at the top
ax_plot.xaxis.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.3)
ax_plot.set_xlabel("Mobility Score (100 = Full Equality)", fontweight='bold', color='dimgray')
sns.despine(ax=ax_plot, left=True, top=True, right=True)

# Add numeric labels with matching colors
for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
    ax_plot.text(bar.get_width() + 3, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
                 f"{int(bar.get_width())}", va='center', fontweight='black',
                 color=colors[i], fontsize=12)

ax_plot.set_title("Average Legal Mobility Score by Region (2024)",
                  loc='left', fontweight='black', size=18, pad=25, color='#2D3436')

# Step 6: Narrative Text Panel
ax_text.axis('off')
ax_text.text(0, 1.0, "THE GEOGRAPHY OF RESTRICTION", fontsize=15, fontweight='black', va='top')

ax_text.text(0, 0.88, "● The Perfection Rim:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#6C5CE7')
ax_text.text(0, 0.84, "High Income regions have reached\nnominal parity. The focus here shifts\nfrom 'changing laws' to 'enforcing\npractice' and social norms.",
             fontsize=11, va='top')

ax_text.text(0, 0.65, "● The Reform Middle:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#FDCB6E')
ax_text.text(0, 0.61, "East Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa\nare in a transition phase. Many\nnations have removed travel bans\nbut still require permission for\npassports.",
             fontsize=11, va='top')

ax_text.text(0, 0.42, "● The Critical Barrier:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#D63031')
ax_text.text(0, 0.38, "MENA economies show the most\nsevere 'indent' in rights. In these\nareas, legal restrictions on moving\nhouse or traveling abroad remain\nsystemic.",
             fontsize=11, va='top')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

2. The Stagnation of Global Reform¶

Tracking the global average over the last decade reveals a troubling plateau in legal reform.

In [ ]:
# Step 1: Data Setup
years = list(range(2014, 2025))
global_scores = [70, 72, 74, 75, 76, 76.5, 77, 77.2, 77.5, 77.8, 78]

# Step 2: Configure layout architecture
fig, (ax_plot, ax_text) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 7), gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [2.5, 1]})

# Step 3: Render time-series with Color and Gradient
line_color = '#0984E3'
marker_color = '#E17055'


ax_plot.fill_between(years, global_scores, 50, color=line_color, alpha=0.1)

# Plot the main line
ax_plot.plot(years, global_scores, color=line_color, lw=4, zorder=2)


ax_plot.scatter(years, global_scores, color=marker_color, s=100, edgecolor='white', linewidth=2, zorder=3)


ax_plot.set_ylim(65, 85) # Tighter bounds to make the plateau more visible
ax_plot.set_ylabel("Global Average Score", color='dimgray', fontweight='bold', size=12)
ax_plot.xaxis.grid(True, linestyle='--', color='lightgray', alpha=0.5)
ax_plot.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle='--', color='lightgray', alpha=0.5)
ax_plot.set_xticks(years)
sns.despine(ax=ax_plot, top=True, right=True)

ax_plot.set_title("Global Average Mobility Score: 10-Year Momentum",
                  loc='left', fontweight='black', size=18, pad=25, color='#2D3436')


ax_text.axis('off')
ax_text.text(0, 1.0, "A TROUBLING PLATEAU", fontsize=15, fontweight='black', va='top', color='#2D3436')

ax_text.text(0, 0.88, "● The 2014-2018 Surge:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color=line_color)
ax_text.text(0, 0.84, "Notice the steep initial climb.\nThis period saw rapid legislative\nrepeals across multiple regions.",
             fontsize=11, va='top', linespacing=1.4)

ax_text.text(0, 0.65, "● The Stagnation Point:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color=marker_color)
ax_text.text(0, 0.61, "Post-2019, the curve flattens.\nDespite global advocacy, the rate\nof new mobility laws has slowed\nto a crawl.",
             fontsize=11, va='top', linespacing=1.4)

ax_text.text(0, 0.42, "● The 2025 Outlook:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#636E72')
ax_text.text(0, 0.38, "At the current trajectory, it will\ntake decades to reach 100%.\nThe plateau suggests we have hit\na 'policy wall'.",
             fontsize=11, va='top', linespacing=1.4)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

3. The Passport Gap¶

Nearly half of the world's economies still enforce legal barriers restricting women from obtaining passports.

In [ ]:
# Step 1: Data Setup

counts = [85, 105]

# Step 3: Render the Donut Chart

    counts,
    labels=None,
    autopct='%1.1f%%',

    colors=colors,
    pctdistance=0.85,

    wedgeprops={'width': 0.4, 'edgecolor': 'w', 'linewidth': 3}
)


for autotext in autotexts:

    autotext.set_weight('bold')
    autotext.set_fontsize(14)

ax_text.text(0, 0.61, f"{counts[1]} nations (the green slice)\nhave successfully codified full\nmobility, showing that legal parity\nis a globally achievable norm.",

4. Household Head Dynamics¶

Laws frequently dictate that a woman cannot choose where to live, severely limiting her economic agency.

5. Generational Mobility¶

When women cannot pass citizenship to their spouses or children, mobility restrictions become generational.

In [ ]:
# Step 1
total = 190
equal = 120
unequal = 70

# Colors
color_equal = '#00CEC9'   # Bright Teal
color_unequal = '#E17055' # Burnt Orange

# Step 2: Configure layout (70% Plot, 30% Narrative)
fig, (ax_plot, ax_text) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 7), gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [2, 1]})

# Step 3: Draw the Grid (10 rows x 19 columns)
rows = 10
cols = 19
count = 0

for r in range(rows):
    for c in range(cols):
        if count < equal:
            color = color_equal
        else:
            color = color_unequal

        # Draw a "person" or "passport" proxy (circle + square)
        circle = mpatches.Circle((c, rows - r), 0.3, color=color)
        ax_plot.add_patch(circle)
        count += 1

# Step 4: Visual Styling
ax_plot.set_xlim(-1, cols)
ax_plot.set_ylim(0, rows + 1)
ax_plot.set_aspect('equal')
ax_plot.axis('off')

ax_plot.set_title("The Global Citizenship Grid: Each Dot = 1 Economy",
                  loc='left', fontweight='black', size=18, pad=20, color='#2D3436')

# Custom Legend
equal_patch = mpatches.Patch(color=color_equal, label=f'Equal Rights ({equal})')
unequal_patch = mpatches.Patch(color=color_unequal, label=f'Unequal Rights ({unequal})')
ax_plot.legend(handles=[equal_patch, unequal_patch], loc='lower left',
               bbox_to_anchor=(0, -0.1), ncol=2, frameon=False, prop={'weight':'bold'})

# Step 5: Narrative Text Panel
ax_text.axis('off')
ax_text.text(0, 1.0, "IMPORTED RESTRICTIONS", fontsize=16, fontweight='black', va='top', color='#2D3436')

ax_text.text(0, 0.88, "● The Global Mosaic:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color=color_equal)
ax_text.text(0, 0.84, f"The teal dots represent the {equal}\nnations that have decoupled\ngender from nationality, allowing\nmothers to pass citizenship freely.",

ax_text.text(0, 0.38, "● Beyond the Border:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#636E72')

6. The Wealth Divide in Mobility¶

Mobility rights are heavily correlated with national income levels, trapping women in lower-income economies.

In [ ]:

7. Momentum for Change¶

Despite the plateau, several nations have aggressively rewritten their laws in the last 5 years.

In [ ]:
# Step 1
reformers = ['Saudi Arabia', 'UAE', 'Togo']
start_score = [25, 30, 40]
end_score = [100, 100, 100]

# Step 2: Configure layout architecture
fig, (ax_plot, ax_text) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 7), gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [2.5, 1]})

# Define a vibrant, unique color palette for each country's path
# Deep Purple, Emerald Green, and Electric Blue
path_colors = ['#6C5CE7', '#00B894', '#0984E3']
start_point_color = '#E17055' # Sunset Orange for historical baseline
end_point_color = '#2D3436'   # Obsidian for the finished achievement

# Step 3: Render the Colorful Dumbbell Plot
for i, country in enumerate(reformers):
    # Draw the colorful connecting line
    ax_plot.plot([start_score[i], end_score[i]], [i, i], color=path_colors[i], lw=5, alpha=0.6, zorder=1)

    # Plot Start Score (Past)
    ax_plot.scatter(start_score[i], i, color=start_point_color, s=180, edgecolor='white', linewidth=2, zorder=3)

    # Plot End Score (Present)
    ax_plot.scatter(end_score[i], i, color=path_colors[i], s=180, edgecolor='white', linewidth=2, zorder=3)

    # Add Start score labels (Historical)
    ax_plot.text(start_score[i] - 4, i, f"{start_score[i]}", va='center', ha='right',
                 fontweight='black', color=start_point_color, fontsize=11)

    # Add End score labels (100% Milestone)
    ax_plot.text(end_score[i] + 4, i, f"{end_score[i]}", va='center', ha='left',
                 fontweight='black', color=path_colors[i], fontsize=11)

# Step 4: Visual Styling
ax_plot.set_xlim(0, 120)
ax_plot.xaxis.grid(True, linestyle='--', color='lightgray', alpha=0.5)
ax_plot.set_xlabel("Mobility Score Progress (0-100)", color='dimgray', fontweight='bold', labelpad=15)
ax_plot.set_yticks(range(len(reformers)))
ax_plot.set_yticklabels(reformers, fontweight='black', fontsize=13, color='#2D3436')
sns.despine(ax=ax_plot, top=True, right=True, left=True)

ax_plot.set_title("The Great Reform Sprint: Rapid Legal Leap (Last 5 Years)",
                  loc='left', fontweight='black', size=18, pad=30, color='#2D3436')

# Step 5: Enhanced Narrative Panel
ax_text.axis('off')
ax_text.text(0, 1.0, "RAPID REFORM IS POSSIBLE", fontsize=15, fontweight='black', va='top', color='#2D3436')

ax_text.text(0, 0.88, "● The Historical Baseline:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color=start_point_color)
ax_text.text(0, 0.84, "The orange markers represent the\nrestrictive legal landscape these\nnations faced just five years ago.",
             fontsize=11, va='top', linespacing=1.4)

ax_text.text(0, 0.65, "● The Momentum Path:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#636E72')
ax_text.text(0, 0.61, "The colored bars show the scale of\nreform. These nations closed the\ngap by 60-75 points in record\ntime.",
             fontsize=11, va='top', linespacing=1.4)

ax_text.text(0, 0.42, "● The Result:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#00B894')
ax_text.text(0, 0.38, "By 2024, Saudi Arabia, UAE, and\nTogo have reached full legal parity\nin mobility, serving as a global\nblueprint for change.",
             fontsize=11, va='top', linespacing=1.4)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

8.Regional Disparities in Women's Mobility Rights¶

This Lollipop Chart isolates the global extremes, contrasting the "Perfection Rim" of High-Income regions against the "Critical Gaps" in MENA and South Asia to pinpoint exactly where legislative reform is most urgent.

In [ ]:
# Step 0:
df_lollipop = df.copy()
df_lollipop['OBS_VALUE_NUM'] = pd.to_numeric(df_lollipop['OBS_VALUE'], errors='coerce')
df_lollipop['TIME_PERIOD'] = pd.to_numeric(df_lollipop['TIME_PERIOD'], errors='coerce')
df_lollipop = df_lollipop.dropna(subset=['OBS_VALUE_NUM', 'REF_AREA_LABEL', 'TIME_PERIOD'])

latest_year = int(df_lollipop['TIME_PERIOD'].max())
df_latest_year = df_lollipop[df_lollipop['TIME_PERIOD'] == latest_year]
df_latest_year = df_latest_year.groupby('REF_AREA_LABEL')['OBS_VALUE_NUM'].mean().reset_index()

# Step 1: Isolate the extremes
top5 = df_latest_year.nlargest(5, 'OBS_VALUE_NUM')
bottom5 = df_latest_year.nsmallest(5, 'OBS_VALUE_NUM')
df_display = pd.concat([top5, bottom5]).sort_values('OBS_VALUE_NUM', ascending=True)

# Step 2: Create a vibrant color gradient (
my_cmap = plt.get_cmap("RdYlBu")
rescale = lambda y: (y - np.min(y)) / (np.max(y) - np.min(y))
colors = my_cmap(rescale(df_display['OBS_VALUE_NUM']))

# Step 3: Plot dual-panel layout
fig, (ax_plot, ax_text) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 8), gridspec_kw={'width_ratios': [2.5, 1]})

# Step 4: Draw the colorful Lollipop Chart

ax_plot.hlines(y=df_display['REF_AREA_LABEL'], xmin=0, xmax=df_display['OBS_VALUE_NUM'],
               color=colors, alpha=0.6, linewidth=4)


ax_plot.scatter(df_display['OBS_VALUE_NUM'], df_display['REF_AREA_LABEL'],
                color=colors, s=250, zorder=3, edgecolor='white', linewidth=2)

# Step 5: Add value labels next to the circles for clarity
for i, row in df_display.reset_index().iterrows():
    ax_plot.text(row['OBS_VALUE_NUM'] + 2, i, f"{row['OBS_VALUE_NUM']:.1f}",
                 va='center', fontweight='black', color=colors[i], fontsize=12)

# Axis Styling
ax_plot.set_xlim(0, 115)
ax_plot.set_xlabel("Average Mobility Score (0–100)", fontweight='bold', color='dimgray', labelpad=15)
ax_plot.set_ylabel("") # Cleaned up for readability
ax_plot.set_title(f"The Global Mobility Divide: Top & Bottom Regions ({latest_year})",
                  fontweight='black', size=20, loc='left', pad=30, color='#2D3436')
ax_plot.xaxis.grid(True, linestyle='--', color='lightgray', alpha=0.5)
sns.despine(ax=ax_plot, left=True, top=True, right=True)

# Step 6: Narrative Panel with context
ax_text.axis('off')
ax_text.text(0, 1.0, "REGIONAL DISPARITIES", fontsize=16, fontweight='black', va='top', color='#2D3436')

ax_text.text(0, 0.88, "● The Leading Edge:", fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#4834D4')

]

)

# Step 0:
df_radar = df_latest.copy()

# Step 1: Prepare coordinates for the Radar/Spider Chart
labels = df_radar['Region'].values
stats = df_radar['Mobility_Score'].values

# To close the circular loop, we repeat the first value at the end
angles = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, len(labels), endpoint=False).tolist()
stats = np.concatenate((stats, [stats[0]]))
angles += angles[:1]

# Step 2: Initialize Layout
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 8))
ax_plot = fig.add_axes([0.05, 0.1, 0.6, 0.8], polar=True)
ax_text = fig.add_axes([0.7, 0.1, 0.25, 0.8])

# Step 3: Draw the Radar Plot
ax_plot.fill(angles, stats, color='#6C5CE7', alpha=0.25)
ax_plot.plot(angles, stats, color='#6C5CE7', linewidth=4, marker='o', markersize=8)

# Step 4: Styling the Circular Grid
ax_plot.set_yticklabels([]) # Hide numeric labels for a cleaner look
ax_plot.set_xticks(angles[:-1])
ax_plot.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color='#2D3436')
ax_plot.set_title("Global Mobility Rights Profile (2024)",
                  fontweight='black', size=16, pad=40, color='#2C3E50')

# Step 5: Narrative text panel with color-coded context

9. Final Discussion and Conclusion¶

Strengths of the Analysis Pipeline¶

  • Objective Baseline: Utilizing the World Bank's legal framework provides an unarguable, objective baseline of de jure (in law) restrictions, completely removing subjective survey bias.
  • Pre-attentive Clarity: By stripping away traditional chart clutter and utilizing isolated text annotations, the pipeline forces the audience to focus strictly on actionable data gaps rather than aesthetic noise.

Limitations of the Approach¶

  • De Jure vs. De Facto: This dataset strictly measures laws on the books. It does not measure actual enforcement. A country might score 100/100 in legal mobility, but cultural or economic barriers may still severely restrict women in practice.
  • Lack of Granularity: The data is aggregated at the national level. This masks severe regional, rural-vs-urban, or provincial inequalities that exist within large economies.

Data-Driven Recommendations for the Client (NGOs & Policymakers)¶

  1. Pivot Funding to "Passport Gaps": The 5-year stagnation in the global trend line proves that general awareness campaigns are yielding diminishing returns. Development funds must be redirected into aggressive, targeted legal lobbying in the 85 economies that still restrict passport and travel rights.
  2. Leverage the "Reformer Blueprint": Nations like Togo and Saudi Arabia have proven that rapid legislative overhaul is possible. NGOs should package their recent legislative frameworks as "turn-key" templates for neighboring low-performing nations.
  3. Condition Infrastructure Grants: International organizations must condition future physical infrastructure grants on the implementation of gender-sensitive safety policies, directly addressing the massive 160-nation blind spot in public transit.
